description:
Elixir 1.19.4 (builder's probes): backslash-x with two hex digits is a RAW BYTE, not a code point: "\xFF" is <<255>>, "\xe9" is <<233>>, exactly two digits are read ("\x414" is <<65, 52>>). One digit is accepted with a deprecation warning. The braced form is a code point encoded as UTF-8 ("\x{e9}" is <<195, 169>>), deprecated with a warning; out-of-range and surrogate values give 'invalid or reserved Unicode code point'; malformed forms give 'invalid hex escape character, expected \xHH where H is a hexadecimal digit'. Heredocs the same. In a quoted atom or keyword key a byte that is not valid UTF-8 is an 'invalid encoding' error. ?\x41 is a syntax error.
Why the first attempt stopped: Lexer::read_escape returns a char and a raw byte above 0x7F is not one. What has to change: read_escape returns a character or a byte; string and heredoc parts (already byte vectors, StringPart::Bytes) push the byte; the quoted-atom and keyword-key paths reject a byte that breaks UTF-8; ?\x stays an error. Elixir's two deprecation warnings have no channel in fz's lexer: decide error or accept. A string holding a non-UTF-8 byte is new for fz: check what printing, String functions and inspect do with it on all three paths before building. Fixtures 01225-01229 are free.

DECIDED 2026-11-13 by the user: follow Elixir. Backslash-x with two hex digits is a raw byte, so a string may hold bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
title: Strings accept Elixir's hex escapes
